newsitem.title: USA: IMM currency futures end erratic trade mixed.
newsitem.headline: IMM currency futures end erratic trade mixed.

text.p: IMM currency futures ended a session of erratic pit trading mixed as the market prepared for Friday's February U.S. employment figures.
Nonfarm payrolls are expected on average to rise 230,000, with 5.3-percent joblessness, a 0.4-percent rise in hourly earnings and an increase in the workweek to 34.6 hours.

Traders said figures on the high side of estimates - Reuter's payrolls forecasts range from up 118,000 to up 325,000 - plus any signs of more wage-induced inflation than expected would highlight the growing sense that the U.S.'s economy is in substantially better shape than Germany's.
Currencies cut losses and drifted back up toward session peaks late as some shorts apparently evened up in case the jobs figures are not as dollar-bullish as pundits expected.
But few brokers disputed signs that the mark in particular appeared more prone to a further fall vis-a-vis the dollar.

"I think the way the U.S. economy is rolling, we're basically headed in the right direction," said one currency floor broker of the dollar's upside tilt. "I just can't see the (employment) numbers changing that much...(and) the sentiment has to be bearish currencies. There's really nothing we see to stop us from 1.85, even 1.90."
Although adjusted German employment figures Thursday were not as economically weak as rumored early this week, they little more than fleeting support to the mark, brokers said.
March marks retested and held their overnight low at $0.5813, the third consecutive contract low in three days, before the contract drited upward much of the afternoon on light to moderate turnover.

Yen, however, found a modicum of support in crosses and against the U.S. unit as brokers discerned growing concern from U.S. officials about signs that Japan's trade and current account surpluses may be headed back up again.
U.S. Treasury secretary Robert Rubin said near midday that a sustained current account surplus by Japan "was in nobody's interest."
Traders also said calendar spread trades picked up before next week, when the roll into June and out of March begins in earnest. June futures become new lead months on Monday.

March yen ended up $0.000006 at $0.008266, marks eased $0.0010 to $0.5833, Swiss francs ended flat at $0.6757, sterling rose $0.0024 to $1.6152, Canadian dollar rose $0.0024 to $0.7335, Australian dollar gained $0.0026 to $0.7873, Mexican peso ended unchanged at $0.123900.
